findings.F1: The move per case is smaller than the cost of a trade, so the book loses before any other effect. The total move is +0.07 % per case over 6 hours against a cost of 0.11 % per trade. Per day, BTC's gross gain is 0.032 % against 0.078 % of fees. ETH's gross gain is 0.062 % against 0.062 % of fees. The book's mean daily return is -0.025 %.
findings.F2: On BTC the book does no timing at all. The gain from the market's own rise (0.031 % a day) equals almost all of its gross gain (0.032 % a day). On ETH, timing adds only 0.034 % a day of its 0.062 %.
findings.F3: The deepest falls get the largest positions, and the trades on them earn the least. Trades entered at forecast 10 to 20 number 6763, more than half of the 12736 trades, and earn +0.046 % gross and -0.054 % net. Trades entered at forecast 2 to 5 earn +0.32 % gross and +0.22 % net (n 3233). Trades entered at forecast 5 to 10 earn +0.23 % gross and +0.13 % net (n 2730). This matches the failed supporting check (upper minus lower half -0.022 %).

findings.F6: Falls on volume below 2/3 of its 30-day average recover more than falls on volume near its average, though the samples are small. For falls of 1.5 to 2 usual moves, the move is +0.28 % (t 1.9, n 222) against +0.11 % (n 316). For falls of 3 to 4 usual moves, it is +1.27 % (t 3.2, n 8) against +0.32 % (n 74).

ideas.idea: After an hour in which the coin falls far more than its typical hourly move over the past 30 days while its volume stays near its average hourly volume over the past 30 days, the price recovers part of that fall over the next two to six hours, only while the coin's 24-hour return before that hour is a rise; the larger that prior 24-hour rise, the larger the recovery.
ideas.consequence: A sharp quiet-volume dip inside a rising day is a pullback worth buying, and a dip that is not inside a rising day is a reason to stay out.
ideas.name: quiet dip in rising day

ideas.idea: After an hour in which the coin falls far more than its typical hourly move over the past 30 days while its volume stays near its average hourly volume over the past 30 days, the price recovers part of that fall over the next two to six hours; the further that hour's volume lies below its 30-day hourly average, the larger the recovery.
ideas.consequence: The thinner the volume behind a sharp hourly fall, the more of that fall a trader can expect to be given back within six hours.
ideas.name: thinner volume, larger fade
